response.markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **protected-recent prefix dropout** within corrected BERT4Rec, after repairing diagnostic category identity. No improvement is established: the supplied curriculum scored 0.5375 versus baseline 0.5425.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Separately normalized branches make objective weights explicit; preserve their reductions across arms. (2) Scheduling requires an exposure-matched constant control; existing scores establish no scheduling benefit. (3) Invalid ModelView.dataset_name blocked serving verification before scoring, leaving stale-history dependence unmeasured.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec already includes terminal supervision [1]. (2) CL4SRec and CBiT establish context perturbation, while augmentation-only research motivates avoiding an additional contrastive objective [4–6]. (3) IeSRec explicitly removes oldest interactions [7]; recency protection has limited novelty. Recency Sampling and Q-BERT4Rec motivate target alignment and corruption studies, without establishing this policy’s benefit [2,3].

**Framework.** Three directions separate mechanisms: objective allocation changes loss emphasis; context selection changes available evidence; representation enrichment changes item information. Within context selection, distinguish generic regularization, recency protection, and contiguous cropping. Hold objectives and representations fixed.

Candidate assessments use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=difficulty; higher D means harder. Each score includes a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matched-mean constant terminal weight [1] | 2: attributable; established | 5: useful control; narrow | 5: inference alignment; indirect | 5: tests separation; pooled margins | 2: scalar change; paired sampling |
| Protected-recent prefix dropout [4–7] | 3: precise policy; close precedents | 6: cheap mechanism test; context loss | 7: stale/broad cues; purpose unobserved | 6: margin robustness; sensitivity unavailable | 4: no parameters; masking/control integration |
| Joint title residual encoder | 4: compliant combination; established fusion | 6: sparse-item sharing; extra cost | 6: specific wording; lexical shortcuts | 4: richer features; no content diagnostic | 6: one network; vocabulary/export work |

**Selected idea.** On terminal examples, draw a deletion count from Bernoulli trials over positions preceding the final two history items. Delete exactly that many older positions, replacing them with attention-masked PAD holes. Preserve absolute positions, recent items, target and final MASK. Compare unchanged training, matched-count uniform deletion, and protected deletion; prioritize the latter comparison to distinguish recency protection from regularization. Optional oldest-prefix and recent-only deletion use identical counts.

Two user-facing hypotheses are reduced influence of outdated interests and fewer broad historical associations outranking specific recent matches. Purpose remains unobserved. The model-facing target is sampled-pair ranking errors, approximately 4.0–5.7%; Electronics’ tenth-percentile margin is 0.683. These pooled training statistics establish neither terminal-specific weakness nor validation gains.

Repair category identity, verify serialized/exported parity, and retain frozen diagnostic panels. Preserve seeds, routing, training limits and coefficient schedule. Disable nested conversion where applicable; verify PAD-mask polarity and final-mask readout [8–10]. Select solely through pinned macro validation HR@10. Record evaluated alternatives and conditional paired intervals where available; sampled gains do not establish full-catalog superiority or remove selection bias [11,12]. Train and serve one model/checkpoint per category; never combine arms.

idea.description: Protected-recent prefix dropout with matched deletion-count controls: regularize the terminal-prefix branch of corrected BERT4Rec by removing a small fraction of older visible context while preserving its two most recent history items. Compare against uniform deletion with the identical per-example removal count. Each experimental arm trains exactly one independent model per category and serves exactly one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies outdated interests and broad associations displacing specific current matches. Selectively corrupting older context may reduce reliance on these cues while preserving recent evidence, although recent events need not reveal current purpose. The model-facing hypothesis is improved sampled positive–negative separation, particularly the weaker Electronics margin tail. Supplied errors are pooled in-sample measurements, not terminal-specific estimates or validation improvements. Serving parity and history sensitivity remain unavailable because category identity is invalid. The prior curriculum's supplied validation score is below baseline. Close augmentation and oldest-history deletion precedents reduce originality; the contribution is a carefully controlled BERT4Rec experiment, not a new learning principle.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected BERT4Rec architecture and canonical predictor writer. Apply augmentation only to terminal examples after leakage-free prefix construction and before log2feats. Let n be the number of real visible history positions and q=max(n-2,0). Draw k~Binomial(q,0.15) independently per example. In the protected arm, choose k positions uniformly without replacement from the q positions preceding the latest two history items. This is distributionally equivalent to independent 15% deletion of those older positions. In the matched uniform arm, choose k positions uniformly without replacement from all n visible positions. Pair k exactly across arms using dedicated RNG streams. Short prefixes with at most two visible items have k=0 in every arm. This deliberate choice gives uniform deletion the same intervention dose; it is not unconditional 15% deletion over all history positions.

Replace selected IDs with PAD=0. Do not compact, backfill, reindex surviving positions, alter labels, or remove the final reserved MASK. Preserve the baseline absolute position convention; if positions are derived from cumulative nonpadding counts, compute the original position IDs before augmentation and retain them. A changed position convention must also update configuration, model factory and predictor writer consistently. Remove the target occurrence and all later interactions before augmentation; earlier repeated target IDs remain legitimate observed history. The terminal target, supervised-position count, interior examples, loss reductions, negative proposal and exclusions remain identical across arms. Record n, q, k, removed indices, realized deletion rates and the frequency of unmodified examples. Do not condition deletion on model scores, target identity, validation outcomes or unavailable semantic labels.

Prespecify three arms: unchanged training, matched-count uniform deletion, and protected deletion. At 30% research progress, prioritize the protected-versus-uniform comparison after the shared integration repair; include a fresh unchanged arm only if budget permits. If the unchanged arm cannot run, report that limitation and do not attribute differences from historical scores solely to augmentation. Optional oldest-prefix and recent-only controls remove the earliest or latest k visible positions, respectively, into the same fixed-position PAD holes. Thus oldest-prefix deletion tests contiguous versus scattered removal under matched positions; compacted prefix cropping is a different intervention and requires its own position-reassignment control. Do not sweep deletion probability or suffix protection initially. Any later suffix sweep must hold each example's deletion count fixed and restrict k to the eligibility bound shared by every compared suffix length.

Retain the supplied objective schedule exactly: alpha(e)=0.5+0.3*min(e/100,1), with zero-based epochs and the same configured epoch count in every arm. Compute terminal and interior losses by averaging supervised positions within each example and then examples within each branch. Optimize alpha*Lt+(1-alpha)*Li. This estimates augmentation effects conditional on the existing schedule, not an advantage of scheduling. Retain the earlier matched-mean constant-weight experiment as a separate objective-allocation direction; do not combine it with augmentation in the first comparison. Keep optimizer, learning-rate schedule, regularization, initialization, users, endpoints, interior masks, negatives, branch sizes, updates and checkpoint opportunities fixed. Dedicated RNG streams must keep augmentation from advancing sampling, initialization or model-dropout RNG differently. The supplied helper consumes the same augmentation draws in all modes, including the unchanged control.

PAD holes must exclude keys throughout every attention layer. With MultiheadAttention, boolean True means ignore/block; with functional scaled_dot_product_attention, boolean True means allow. For direct SDPA on B x H x L x D features, the allowed-key mask is (~pad_mask)[:,None,None,:]. Float masks use zero for allowed entries and negative infinity for blocked entries. Set SDPA dropout_p=0.0 in evaluation explicitly. Key masking does not force padded-query outputs to zero: exclude PAD-query outputs from losses and readout and verify finite valid-query features. For TransformerEncoder, use enable_nested_tensor=False where applicable to preserve dense slots predictably; inspect compatibility with the installed implementation rather than assuming automatic nested conversion preserves holes. These requirements follow from supplied documentation, not a local execution. If fixing an existing attention defect is necessary, apply the identical repair to every arm and treat the repaired model as the common control.

Before interpreting diagnostics, set ModelView.dataset_name to the actual routed category. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual trained view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Validate prefix provenance during construction; tensors alone cannot establish provenance or uniform negative sampling. Keep common frozen diagnostic panels unaugmented and separate from training RNG. Report terminal and interior margins separately, with counts and definitions. A matched frozen corruption panel can describe robustness but is not host validation. Retain unavailable flags for history sensitivity and residual patching until their existing gates pass; do not infer collapse from embedding measurements near 0.5.

Verify exact checkpoint state identity and finite float32 scores across the trained module, factory reload, ModelView and exported working/predict.py. Cover short, full-length, overlength/truncated and mixed-length inputs, singleton/batch agreement, internal PAD holes and unmodified serving histories. Check attention behavior in training and evaluation modes; compare deterministic numerical parity in eval mode with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 and the existing deterministic ranking checks. Appended-mask readout is features[:, -1] for fixed-width examples. A general readout uses the greatest nonpadding index, never nonpadding_count-1. Store vocabulary mapping, PAD/MASK IDs, maxlen, position conventions and architecture configuration with the selected state_dict; rebuild with strict loading. No new inference augmentation or stochastic prediction is introduced.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl and their routing; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Respect the supplied environment epoch default of 200. Use one GPU and trial-local artifacts. All controls, diagnostics and failed attempts count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Prespecify identical resource caps and checkpoint opportunities; record actual updates, target counts, GPU seconds and incomplete runs. Do not treat unequal completed runs as a controlled comparison. The host's pinned macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection criterion. Export one selected checkpoint per category from the chosen trial; never average checkpoints, fuse scores or reuse other trials' trained checkpoints.

If the existing host output exposes paired user hit indicators, bootstrap the same user indices for both models independently within each category, then average the four category differences equally. Prespecify 500 CPU bootstrap replicates with seed 42 and report a percentile 95% interval. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR@10 by 0.005 and macro HR@10 by 0.00125. Intervals condition on fixed candidates and fitted checkpoints; they exclude training and candidate-sampling variability. Do not modify the evaluator or fabricate per-user outcomes if unavailable. Record every evaluated hypothesis and checkpoint opportunity. Post-selection intervals do not remove repeated-validation optimism. HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives cannot establish full-catalog HR@10 superiority; the twenty-user full-catalog simulator remains a separate qualitative diagnostic with uncertain judgments recorded separately.

Only public histories, titles, descriptions and historical timestamps are available; this experiment uses histories alone. Do not use ratings, reviews, item categories/prices/stores, simulator traits, unknown target timestamps, extra data or pretrained weights. Do not infer ownership, compatibility, fulfilled needs or current purpose. The proposal does not directly solve duplicate-supply recommendations. Shortcut risks include overreliance on the latest item, popularity, prefix length and artificial PAD patterns; older context may encode durable preferences. Describe available training-derived history-length/frequency strata and frozen recent-versus-older interventions without changing selection metrics. A gain over unchanged training alone supports augmentation, while a gain over matched uniform deletion is more specific evidence for selective recency protection; neither proves the simulator's proposed behavioral mechanism.

User Diagnosis Alignment: 7/10. Positive: explicitly targets outdated interests and broad association shortcuts, satisfying two identified user-facing failure modes. Negative: recent context is an imperfect proxy for specific purpose, and durable preferences may be lost. Model Diagnosis Alignment: 6/10. Positive: tests robustness and sampled ranking errors with controlled margins and parity-gated sensitivity. Negative: existing history dependence is unmeasured and in-sample margin changes need not predict host HR@10. No baseline source was supplied here; the code is an integration helper rather than a standalone replacement train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch


def protected_recent_dropout(sequence, mask_id, augmentation_generator,
                             p=0.15, mode='protected'):
    """Terminal rows only; CPU B x L integer tensor.

    Modes: none, uniform, protected, oldest, recent.
    Use identically seeded dedicated generators and identical incoming
    terminal batches across arms. Returns augmented IDs and deleted mask.
    Original absolute position IDs must be retained by the model/caller.
    """
    modes = {'none', 'uniform', 'protected', 'oldest', 'recent'}
    if mode not in modes or not 0.0 <= p <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError('Invalid augmentation mode or probability')
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or sequence.shape[1] < 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected B x L terminal sequences')
    if sequence.device.type != 'cpu':
        raise ValueError('Use the dedicated CPU augmentation stream')
    if not 1 < mask_id:
        raise ValueError('MASK must follow the real item vocabulary')
    if not torch.all(sequence.ge(0) & sequence.le(mask_id)):
        raise ValueError('Invalid token ID')
    if not torch.all(sequence[:, -1].eq(mask_id)):
        raise ValueError('Terminal rows must end in reserved MASK')
    if not torch.all(sequence.eq(mask_id).sum(dim=1).eq(1)):
        raise ValueError('Expected exactly one terminal MASK per row')

    visible = sequence.gt(0) & sequence.lt(mask_id)
    if not torch.all(visible.any(dim=1)):
        raise ValueError('Every terminal example needs visible history')
    from_right = visible.flip(1).long().cumsum(1).flip(1)
    older = visible & from_right.gt(2)

    # Identical draw shapes and counts in EVERY arm, including no deletion.
    count_draws = torch.rand(sequence.shape,
                             generator=augmentation_generator)
    priority = torch.rand(sequence.shape,
                          generator=augmentation_generator)
    counts = (older & count_draws.lt(p)).sum(dim=1)
    dropped = torch.zeros_like(visible)

    for row in range(sequence.shape[0]):
        k = int(counts[row].item())
        if mode == 'none' or k == 0:
            continue
        eligible = older[row] if mode == 'protected' else visible[row]
        positions = torch.nonzero(eligible, as_tuple=False).flatten()
        if k > positions.numel():
            raise ValueError('Deletion count exceeds eligible positions')
        if mode in {'protected', 'uniform'}:
            order = torch.argsort(priority[row, positions], stable=True)
            selected = positions[order[:k]]
        elif mode == 'oldest':
            selected = positions[:k]
        else:
            selected = positions[-k:]
        dropped[row, selected] = True

    augmented = sequence.clone()
    augmented[dropped] = 0
    assert torch.equal(augmented[:, -1], sequence[:, -1])
    if mode == 'protected':
        assert not torch.any(dropped & visible & from_right.le(2))
    return augmented, dropped

originality.positive: A fixed-position, matched-count comparison isolates selective recency protection within the corrected terminal-prefix BERT4Rec setup.
originality.negative: Context augmentation, Cloze/dropout views and removal of oldest interactions have close precedents; recency protection itself is not broadly novel.

future_potential.positive: A relatively inexpensive controlled comparison could distinguish generic regularization from selective context retention and guide later context-selection research.
future_potential.negative: Durable preferences may be erased, additional controls consume the shared budget, and sampled validation gains would not establish full-catalog usefulness or behavioral causation.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds no parameters or inference computation and can be implemented as a terminal-batch transformation.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact-count controls, paired RNG streams, PAD-hole attention, positional preservation and the existing diagnostic/export integration defect make implementation more demanding than a simple dropout operator.

related_work.title: [1] BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item modeling and appended-mask inference.
Includes terminal-item supervision, providing the family-correct foundation and control.
limitations: Terminal supervision cannot substantiate novelty for this proposal.
Does not establish benefits of protected-recent deletion on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: [2] Recency Sampling for Next-Item Recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary motivates aligning training-target selection with next-item prediction.
limitations: Target sampling and context deletion change different distributions.
Does not establish stale-interest dependence in the supplied model.

related_work.title: [3] Q-BERT4Rec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes span, tail and multi-region masking.
limitations: Multimodal representations and quantization prevent attributing overall results to masking alone.
Provides no matched evidence for the proposed history-only policy.

related_work.title: [4] CL4SRec
contributions: Uses cropping, item masking and local reordering to construct contrastive views.
Establishes context perturbation as relevant prior art.
limitations: Does not specifically establish protected-recent deletion.
Contrastive training differs from the proposed unchanged supervised objective.

related_work.title: [5] CBiT
contributions: Combines Cloze masking and dropout to generate contrastive views in a bidirectional recommendation setting.
limitations: Provides close augmentation precedent rather than evidence for the proposed deletion policy.
Its contrastive components are outside the initial atomic experiment.

related_work.title: [6] Is Contrastive Learning Necessary?
contributions: The supplied search summary reports that direct augmentation can match or outperform some contrastive methods.
Motivates an augmentation-only experiment.
limitations: Does not establish superiority on the pinned four-category BERT4Rec task.

related_work.title: [7] IeSRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes deletion beginning with oldest interactions to emphasize recent behavior.
Provides a close recency precedent and motivates the oldest-prefix control.
limitations: Reduces novelty claims for protecting recent context.
Does not isolate scattered older-position deletion under this benchmark.

related_work.title: [8] PyTorch TransformerEncoder implementation, version 2.5.1
contributions: Documents dense sequence processing and nested-conversion eligibility checks.
Supports disabling nested conversion for predictable handling of left padding and internal holes.
limitations: The installed version and supplied model implementation still require verification.
Source inspection does not establish numerical parity of the actual exported predictor.

related_work.title: [9] PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Specifies boolean padding and attention mask polarity: True ignores or blocks.
limitations: Key masking does not guarantee zero padded-query outputs.

related_work.title: [10] PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention documentation
contributions: Specifies boolean True as an allowed attention connection.
Requires explicitly disabling attention dropout during evaluation.
limitations: Broadcasting, numerical behavior and model integration require actual checks.

related_work.title: [11] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the pinned selection objective.
Applying metric corrections would change the benchmark and is excluded.

related_work.title: [12] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection optimism from repeatedly optimizing noisy validation estimates.
limitations: Does not quantify bias for these particular trials.
Conditional post-selection bootstrap intervals do not remove that bias.

related_work.title: TiCoSeRec
contributions: Uses timestamp gaps to select cropping and masking augmentations.
Motivates comparing structured operators against random counterparts.
limitations: Temporal uniformity differs from protecting recent items and can retain older history.
The proposed experiment does not add timestamp-based selection.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides methodological precedent for paired bootstrap comparison.
Motivates resampling the same evaluation units for both systems.
limitations: Applying it to recommendation requires the category-stratified paired-user procedure specified here.
Intervals exclude training variability, candidate variability and selection bias.
